entries.title: Settling in
entries.text:
Hopefully this damn thing saves what I type this time around. If not, then I'll see if Skippy wants to add it to his scrap heap.

It's been a long few months since we got settled into the Refuge, and every day brings just as much challenge as it does progress. But in spite of it all, just the other day I caught myself starting to feel at home. 

Hadn't realized before how difficult it was to even remember what "home" even felt like, or if I even could. But all the whys and what-ifs in the world won't bring the Responders back. That's *my* job--and for once it looks like I may just have what I need to get it done.

entries.title: Orlando
entries.text:
I've always had an eye for sizing up folks in a hurry. But this Orlando character...they're a tough one to figure. Even worse they seem to like it that way. 

Can't say I got any real idea who these "management" folks are, or even if they really exist at all, but the Responders still aren't in any kind of position to be turning away resources, much less the roof over our own damn heads. 

Dad always used to say that the proper way to thank someone was with a grateful heart, and a wary mind. Like most else in life, he was right. 

So...thank you, Orlando. Now what's in it for you?

entries.title: Refuge
entries.text:
I can't imagine what kind of trading post would've needed as much space as the Whitespring did, but Skippy says there were places just like it all over the country before the bombs fell. Though he says all kinds of crazy stuff. 

Guessing the robots here were what kept the place in such decent repair. But it begs a bit of a question--who kept those robots up and running? Maybe they got to repairing each other after a while. 

But hell, if they're capable of that kind of thinking, then I reckon we'd have a very different set of troubles to contend with, and we sure don't need any new ones on top of what we already got.

entries.title: No time to wonder
entries.text:
Never did see anyone fight and plan and push ahead the way dad could. He kept at it right until we'd gotten clear of that last raiding party, and there was this look in his eyes--like he knew that bullet in his side wasn't gonna let him off the hook.

I told myself then I would do everything I could to make sure no one else ever had to see a look like that in their loved one's eyes. But yesterday, I came up short. That kid who crawled up from Charleston with the buckshot and gangrene in his leg...

I know I did what all that could be done. Everyone here did. But sometimes it feels like we're fighting on a new front every damn day: scorched, rads, ghouls, med shortages, busted supplies, not to mention the usual cast of clowns who can't help but shoot at one another. 

Some days it gets tough to remember why I brought the Responders back at all. Today won't be one of those days--just got word of a new patient coming in. 

Time to get back to work.

entries.title: Fire Breathers recruiting
entries.text:
All,

I just wanted to remind everyone that the Fire Breathers unit is always looking for more manpower. 

If you think you've got what it takes to handle our toughest missions and take on the Scorched, then Melody and Madigan would love to meet you.
 
Don't forget, it's a dangerous assignment, but it comes with benefits. You'll have top priority for both rations and ammunition. We ask the Fire Breathers to put their lives on the line, but we reward their bravery where we can.

The job's not for everyone, but if you think you can handle the recruitment process and training, then I ask you to consider signing up.

Thanks,

- Chavez

entries.title: Complaint 15-J
entries.text:
We just received another complaint about the Grafton mayor's office. This time the mayor is being accused of illegally soliciting funds for his reelection campaign. The mayor's assistant allegedly demanded a contribution in exchange for notarizing documents. This one is more serious than the last three. I'd better go check it out.

Followup: An officer was sent to the mayor's office in Grafton. He found some irregularities with the mayor's assistant's procedures. A citation was issued to correct the problem. The officer noted that Grafton's mayor claims there aren't funds to make the changes. We'll let a judge sort it out.

- Larkin

If you haven't met him, he's about six feet tall, brown hair, green eyes, age is about mid-50s. He came in with the last big group refugees.

You might remember him as the electrician who decided to do some unsolicited work on our main computer. I'm sure he meant well, but we had to have him escorted out of the command center. 

Anyway, hopefully he's okay. He borrowed my only screwdriver and I really need it back, so if you see him, send him my way.

- Jeff Nakamura

entries.title: Dealing with the Brotherhood
entries.text:
I've been a member of the Responders almost from the start. Like all of you, I've put my life on the line to save the lives of others more times than I can remember. Our mission is important. That's why we can't let the Brotherhood of Steel push us around.

Of course we'll help anyone where we can, but you all know that our resources are limited. The Brotherhood's been making increasing demands for resources and supplies in the name of holding back the Scorched. 

Well, the Scorched aren't the only threat around here, and the Responders aren't looking to fight a war. We're healers. We're teachers. We're not soldiers.

When the Brotherhood comes asking for your ammo, your stimpaks, your water, whatever it is, think carefully. Someone out there might need those supplies to survive. 

If they ask you to join their ranks because you've got skills they can use, remember that we need those skills just as much, maybe more.

We don't have the benefit of power armor and heavy weapons. All we've got is training, knowledge and courage. But that's been enough so far, and I hope we can keep it that way.

I'm not saying the Brotherhood of Steel is our enemy. We're on the same side. But lately, we're not really friends, either. 

All I'm asking is that you stay focused on the mission - on OUR mission - no matter what they might ask of you.

- Chavez

entries.title: Announcement: Rachel Pryce
entries.text:
Some sad news to share, everyone. 

Some of you might have heard about Rachel already, but for those who don't know, she's said goodbye to the Responders and joined the Brotherhood of Steel to work as a combat medic.

We'll all miss her, and we wish her the best. In the meantime, the few medics we have left are working around the clock. We'll be starting the medical training program up again to help fill in the gaps. Please volunteer if you can spare the time.

- Chavez

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: Hi... Dassa asked me if I would talk about how I got here. She asked everybody. So I said okay. My name is Colonel, and I'm 13 years old.

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: I just wanted to say I'm sorry. I'm sorry for everything... um... the bombs and the messed up people and the cows with two heads. All of it.

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: I was bad... just bad. I cheated on my spelling test, I kicked Chip Wilkins in the shins until he cried, I pushed Rosie McCloy down the stairs...

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: Um... I cut holes in the bottoms of all the gym shorts, and I put glue in the mashed potatoes in the cafeteria...

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: I told Harold Newell to eat ten dead flies a day in order to grow muscles, and um, I put Nuka-Cola in the rat cage water bottles at the pet store...

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: And um... I just wanted to say I'm sorry about everything... because my dad said if I wasn't this way then bad things wouldn't happen...

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: I haven't seen daddy since the bombs and so I guess he left because of that too... It's okay, I am trying to be good now though.

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: *sniffles* I'm not old enough to be a Volunteer but Dassa said I could help collect food and water... so I'm getting better, I promise!

transcript.speaker: Colonel
transcript.text: And um... daddy? If you're listening... I promise I won't be bad anymore so you can come back now. Okay? Okay. Bye. *sniffles*

items.name: Survivor Story: Miguel Caldera
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: Ah, hello person in the distant future! Dassa told us these tapes would be used as historical records someday. Nifty! So, my name is Miguel Caldera.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: Let's see, my story begins in an office. I used to be a programmer at Vault-Tec, one of many. Nobody special, you see. And that's okay.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: I used to stare out that window by the coffee machine and think... shucks, I wish I could leave this job and hike in the woods every day.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: I'd dream about walking the Appalachian trail, setting up camp wherever I liked, and traveling with close friends! Ah.. the dreams kept me going...

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: And well, when the bombs fell... I was terrified just like anybody else. I wasn't in a vault, so I just, you know, had to figure it all out too.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: The Responders found me. I had a little campsite, some supplies. I hacked a protectron to guard me while I slept, but... I missed people. I did!

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: It's been all right, you know? The apocalypse and all. I know that seems weird but... I have freedom now. I can actually help people...

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: I even met somebody - a Volunteer who delivers supplies. Imagine that, right? Even when you think everything is over... it's... it's not. It goes on.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: I mean it's awful too, don't get me wrong. All the people dead and hurt. But, well, those are things beyond my control, so I'm making the best of it.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: These days I'm important. People treat me like I matter because... well, there are so few of us that we can't afford to think otherwise.

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: So, for all you future people... just know that we lived through something... horrible. But we did it. Somehow, we're alive...

transcript.speaker: Miguel Caldera
transcript.text: And if you're hearing this, then well... I guess at least some of us made it. Right? So hey, chin up, kiddo! You'll be okay. Okay?

items.name: Survivor Story: Nurse Scott
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: Responder Dassa gave me some supplies in exchange for my "Survivor Story" so... hi, my name is Scott Shepherd, and things are going all right.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: I was a nurse before the war, and I guess nothing much has changed. I just work for the Responders now, and I don't get paid! Hah!

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: The government is basically the same now as it was years ago. Wrecked. Disorganized. Cannot be trusted. Everyone knows this!

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: You wanna know why the War actually happened? Aliens. You think I'm joking? Listen. Right before everything went to hell... I saw them.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: I was grilling hamburgers out in the yard with my dog and I heard rustling from the bushes, and a zapping noise.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: Next thing I know, I'm light headed and I felt myself falling to the ground... and I didn't even have a lot to drink.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: I woke up and I saw some little thing run into the bushes with my dog following it, and I knew something was wrong.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: I found my dog later with a clump of green skin in his mouth. Green. Like moss or something.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: The bombs fell almost 10 days later. 9 days, 19 hours to be exact. That's 235 hours precisely. You know what that is, right?

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: That's right. The atomic number of the fissile isotope of Uranium -- they had a plan from the very beginning!

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: Why would they come after me first, Scott Shepherd, the nurse? Well. Good question. I'm glad you asked.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: They have our blood! They knew which ones of us would survive. This is one big experiment to them!

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: This whole thing was staged. Our lives. Our thoughts. Everything was designed for us. Just like this conversation. Every word I'm saying.... planned.

transcript.speaker: Scott Shepherd
transcript.text: Time to wake up, Appalachia! Find the ones holding the strings and cut the cords!

items.name: Survivor Story: Tabitha
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: Just talk into this? Oh. Am I loud enough? Okay. Hi... What do you want me to say exactly?

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: Yeah, so just talk about how you got here and maybe a little bit about your life. This is a historic document. Go ahead, Tabitha.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: Okay, so... thanks... okay. I've been sober for 9 days. I got here 9 days ago. My name is Tabitha... and this is my story.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: I just found out about everything. The War, the bombs, I just... I just realized this was uh, really happening.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: For years I thought the chems were playing tricks with my mind... hurting my brain. Thought it was the worst trip ever...

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: Every time I'd come out of my haze long enough to look for food, I'd find more chems... and well... it kept going. And I kept seeing madness.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: Look, I would have been wandering around fighting giant rats and eating garbage if not for the Responders... they're good folks.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: That doc in the Church got me some meds that are helping out a lot, and they have group therapy meetings and... it's good... I think it's helping.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: But listen... you should avoid the mountains. They'll just get you mixed up. Get you doing things you don't wanna do.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: Hurting people mostly... and there are so many chems up there. I spent too long there, and... I hurt people... I couldn't think right... I couldn't.

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: It's okay, Tabitha. Remember what we said in the group? Take your addictol and rest and things will be okay soon. It's okay. We're here for you.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: Yeah... I'm taking it. When I feel better... I'm going out west though. Getting out of this place. Getting away from the chems. All of this.

transcript.speaker: Tabitha
transcript.text: I feel better every day, but... years of chems, years of rads, years of sleeping in the muck... it adds up. I'm gonna get back to sleep now, okay?

transcript.speaker: Dassa Ben-Ami
transcript.text: Okay, thanks for sharing your story, Tabitha. Get some sleep. You'll be okay. You're safe now.

entries.title: Foreman's Log #1
entries.text:
========================
FOREMAN'S LOG - ENTRY #1
========================

Raided the cathedral this morning to hardly any resistance. The Unioners' little "safehouse" was full of weak and sickly civilians. They were counting on the Trench to protect them. But thanks to that new tracker, our whole group got through the radpits without a hitch.

We've got rotating guards on the prisoners while we build a pen for them. I keep hearing them praying. They don't know yet that no god can save them from what I have planned.

entries.title: Foreman's Log #2
entries.text:
========================
FOREMAN'S LOG - ENTRY #2
========================

We drove back the trogs and started building cages underground. But the beasts just keep crawling out of new holes. I'm starting to think we leave them be, make for a little extra security down there... and a convenient way to dispose of underlings who are more of a pain than they're worth. It's not like I ever need to go down there. I'm the god of this temple now. 

That's right. I'm in charge here. I think they're all due for another reminder of that.

entries.title: Foreman's Log #3
entries.text:
========================
FOREMAN'S LOG - ENTRY #3
========================

Everything's set up just the way I like it. Pain and punishment rule this house. We're bringing in new prisoners every day and shaping them up for labor under the Fanatics. They can do our dirty work. Build our bases, gather our supplies, act as body shields. The possibilities are endless if you break them just right.

A few of my lieutenants have gone missing, the tracker among them. He's been more quiet than usual lately, and that's saying a lot. It's a loss, but who cares. There's more where that came from. The rest of those pathetic louts probably got dragged away by trogs.

entries.title: Foreman's Log #4
entries.text:
========================
FOREMAN'S LOG - ENTRY #4
========================

We ousted that asshole! Fed him to the trogs! It's a new dawn for the Sanctum now!

Order won't last long if we don't appoint a new Foreman soon. We're holding a crucible tomorrow. One prisoner to each lieutenant. Whoever gets the best screams rules the Sanctum!

entries.title: Pitt. Union Rail Incident?
entries.text:
To: Edgar Clemmon

Mr Clemmon,

While making my rounds this morning I stopped by the train depot to get a copy of last month's ledger. While there I witnessed a Pittsburgh Union Railroad worker denying this week's waste export. I asked the worker to explain himself, and he said his bosses told him they wouldn't be transporting our waste anymore.

Since I haven't received a memo about this today, I'm hoping it's just a miscommunication on their part. Because we both know how severe an interruption in our waste disposal pipeline is. 

I'm told we have storage for maybe 30 days worth of the stuff, but I can't say I feel comfortable storing it in the same room as the food sanitizer units. If this isn't resolved quickly, we'll have to come up with other ways to dispose of our manufacturing waste.

Regards,
Jacob Doyle
Abraxodyne Complex Product Manager

entries.title: Getting Out of Hand
entries.text:
To: Edgar Clemmon

Pittsburgh Union Railroad still hasn't budged, and I'm starting to get lots of questions from my staff about how we're going to dispose of the waste. To get the Railroad back in our corner, we need to cease all production on PID #31148 until the lab folks can develop a neutralizer. 

You've heard me say it a million times and I'll say it again. Executing this "trial run" without a neutralizer for the waste was a huge mistake. This can't be ignored any longer Edgar.

Regards,
Jacob Doyle
Abraxodyne Complex Product Manager

entries.title: Urgent Memo
entries.text:
To: Product_StaffList

Product Staff,

I have recently confirmed with the management at Pittsburgh Union Railroad that they will no longer be exporting any more byproduct from PID #31148. The waste has been corroding their tank cars, causing damage to both people and property.

Our contract with Pittsburgh Union Railroad had previously allowed us to delay the research and development of the waste neutralizer. With the Union Railroad denying our exports, we can no longer rely on them to handle delivery to our external waste management partners out West. 

Our only solution to get the Union Railroad back on our side is to make the waste safe to store by accelerating our efforts to develop a neutralizer.

Unfortunately, I've been told by leadership that we are forbidden to halt production of PID #31148. It is apparently more important to them that PID #31148 sees an uninterrupted trial run in the hands of our clients. 

In the meantime, waste generated from continued production will be stored in the supply warehouse until further notice. We cannot store it long before we're up to our knees in it however. It is mission critical that we get a working neutralizer as soon as possible.

Meet with your team leads to discuss the next steps. The clock is ticking.

Regards,
Jacob Doyle
Abraxodyne Complex Product Manager

entries.title: My Resignation
entries.text:
To: Product_StaffList

Product Staff,

After all my years of service at Abraxodyne Chemical, recent events have forced me to announce my resignation from my position as Product Manager at the Pittsburgh Abraxodyne Complex. 

Given the right time and resources, I've never seen a challenge this team couldn't tackle. It truly is a shame that management has not seen that same potential. It has been an honor and a privilege to work with everyone here. 

To whoever follows in my stead, I hope you see the same potential in this team that I do. I also hope that you can stand up to the mismanagement of certain leadership, unlike myself. Thank you everyone, and good luck on the challenging road ahead.

Best Regards,
Jacob Doyle

Edgar, have you been reading the incident reports I've been leaving with your secretary? The waste from your plant is nearly melting our tank trains. They've been corroding from the inside, leaking out and getting my folks sick with something fierce. Whatever this stuff is, we're not equipped to handle it. Unless you do something about it, I'm going to have to take drastic action to protect my workers.

Ryan Gilbert,
Yardmaster, Pittsburgh Union Railroad

entries.title: Are you taking this seriously?
entries.text:
To: Edgar Clemmon

Edgar, the barrels you've used in the past were fine when it was just detergent ingredients. But expecting these things to hold up against this mess you all have concocted? It's near impossible to transport safely! I'm not letting any of these on my train cars if you can't prove without a doubt that they won't leak on my trains or my workers.
Frankly, I'm disappointed in you Edgar for trying to get such a lazy solution past me. I thought Abraxodyne and the Pittsburgh Union Railroad had a good relationship. But this low effort attempt at resolving this situation is starting to make me question that.

Ryan Gilbert,
Yardmaster, Pittsburgh Union Railroad

entries.title: Important Change
entries.text:
To: PittsburghUnionRailStaffList

Starting today, we will no longer be handling transportation of industrial waste from the Abraxodyne Complex. Regular shipping and delivery duties will remain unaffected. If you have any questions about this change, please bring them to your supervisor. If you see unauthorized personnel attempting to dump waste into the tank cars, please report them to your supervisor immediately.

Ryan Gilbert,
Yardmaster, Pittsburgh Union Railroad

items.name: Foreman's Terminal
items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.text:
Hal Caldwell : Foreman's Log : 7/31/77

The whole floor's in a tizzy about the new regs put down by ownership last week. Sensing real unrest here, it's getting tense. Been trying to keep the peace as best I can, but hell, even I have to admit they're a step too far this time. We were already busting our asses up and down the line to make quota and now they want triple? Unreal. I don't know what kind of pressure Mr. Mackeson is under to ask that of us, but he'd better have a damn good reason or he's going to be looking at the first strike this foundry has had in twenty years and there'll be nothing we can do to stop it.

Hal Caldwell : Foreman's Log : 9/19/77

Mr. Mackeson finally came by to see what the fuss was about, and the workers let him have it. He should have seen it coming, poor guy. He was not prepared for the vitriol; whoever gives him his reports at HQ should be fired. Had to get the Protectrons involved to keep things from getting out of hand... Not our finest hour.

The boss was clearly shaken, but his orders didn't change. The war effort needs more output, non-negotiable. He didn't rule out "disciplinary action," either. I told him he'd have to fight for it, the union had had enough. He told me it's out of his hands.

Hal Caldwell : Foreman's Log : 10/1/77

Got the union together and we started a dialogue with ownership. Nobody wants a repeat of the labor wars down south in Beckley and Welch. Told Mr. Mackeson that his ask is impossible, and he's sympathetic. He agreed to pull some clever accounting if we can squeeze just a little bit more out of everyone. Hard to say exactly how the rank-and-file will react, but we're hoping to avoid the worst, at least for now.

The longer this war drags on, the harder toll it takes on everyone involved. The grief is hitting us hard, I see it all over the floor. If it's not another relative taken, then it's the guilt of not being out there yourself. I only hope it all ends soon, for all of our sakes.

items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.title: The plan
entries.text:
I don't care what anyone says, we're taking the Foundry back. The other Locals can say what they want about numbers and rations. The 42 ain't no pushovers. And besides that, we've got the brains, don't we? Don't they all say that's what keeps us in the game? The longer we let those bastards occupy the means of production, the more edge we lose in this fight.

I mean, a working foundry in our hands? Pumping out all the gear we could ever want? And meanwhile, the Fanatics are sitting on this goldmine brewing chems and sticking them in weapons... The thought of what our POWs are going through in there makes my blood boil.

So no more "staying on the defensive." If we're going out, we're going out with a bang.

entries.title: Supplies
entries.text:
They hit us hard this time, right where it hurts - in the stomach. Somehow they found our food stores. We're only lucky they didn't have enough hands to haul off with all of it. Still, it's a big blow. Now we're scrambling to refill, hitting everywhere in town that might still have a crumb of unclaimed food left. Meanwhile, Wicker's got his head up his ass worrying about our steel supplies. Weapons and armor don't mean a damn thing if we're too hungry to use them.

The crew was already restless, worn down, and now we have starvation hanging over our heads. There's gotta be a way out of this...

entries.title: Help is on its way
entries.text:
I was tough on Skippy when he left us. I knew he had good intentions, but I didn't think he'd keep his word, that he was just running away like the rest of them that went elsewhere over the years. Well, I was wrong. He's convinced some folks from Appalachia to come lend a helping hand. We've lost so many to the promise of that place; it's ironic to think they could save us.

Skip says they're battle hardened... I guess we'll see about that. Hard to think anyone from down there could be as tough as us, but from the stories he's told... Freaky red ghoul-like things, monster bats, and nukes going off all over. Sounds far-fetched, but if even half of that is true, maybe they'll have a fighting chance here in the Pitt.

items.name: Striker's Log 01: Mission Brief
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: This is Pat Gerber, Striker for the Union. Formerly the 42, now with our command up in the 29. Mission log: taking care of unfinished business.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Used to get reports back in the day of something -- some kind of mutant or monster -- lurking beneath the Foundry.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Disappearances, attacks, one or two mangled corpses... nasty stuff. Thought it was Fanatic raids myself, but panic ensued, so I got put on the case.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Of course, losing the Foundry changed our priorities a bit, but now that we're re-settled, I've come home to take a look.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Can't say I'm not a bit curious... Don't get to monster hunting very often.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Will be a change of pace from rooting out spies and Fanatic guerillas, if indeed it is something new on our plates.

items.name: Striker's Log 02: Pursuit
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Pat Gerber, Union Striker, Local 29. Mission log: in pursuit of a beast. Strange to be back in my old stomping grounds after so long away.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: So much has changed. The streets... well, they've been filthy since the War, of course, but we always used to keep them up as best we could.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Now you can barely move without tripping over old rebar or slipping in a pool of spilled waste... The Fanatics did a number on this place.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Met up with the new Local leader, a woman who goes by Hex.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Guess they've had run-ins with the creatures I'm looking for, so there goes my "Fanatic raider" theory.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: She showed me the body of one of these things... No wonder they had folks running scared.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Going toe-to-toe with these troglodytes would put the fear into anybody. It's a wonder the 42 is still standing.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Best info we have on where they're coming from hasn't changed, though.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Seems disturbances in the Foundry -- raids against the Fanatics -- always stir them up and bring them out of hiding.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Will be quite the task to get in there unnoticed by the enemy, but that's what Strikers are for.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: I know an old route, back door type situation. Should work... If it doesn't, you know where to find my body.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: And send my regards to the rest of the 29. If nothing else, you know I'll take some Fanatics down with me on the way.

items.name: Striker's Log 03: Lion's Den
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Pat Gerber, Union Striker with the Local 29. Mission log: things are getting uncomfortable.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Found a way past the patrols and made it to the tunnels beneath the Foundry.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Place is like a maze, it's no wonder we never scouted the whole thing when we owned this place. And there's evidence of our mutant friends everywhere.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Human bones littered here and there, stripped of all the flesh and muscle... I've got a strong stomach, but it's hard to take.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Must've been dragging folks down here for as long as we suspected. Can't help but think of the friends I've lost...

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: I want to exterminate the whole lot of these creatures.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: The going is getting tougher. No natural light, of course, or artificial for that matter. But more than that, the rads get worse the deeper I go.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: I can feel my body heating up; feel my skin crawling. Stomach is starting to churn, I still haven't found the bastards...

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Pounded some Rad-X, but it's hardly helping. I should know better, but I want to press on.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Maybe a few levels deeper before I turn back and rethink my strategy. Maybe steal a hazmat suit from somewhere, if I'm lucky.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: My damn head's starting to swim... Hope the damage isn't done already.

items.name: Striker's Log 04: Failure
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Pat-- Pat Gerber, uh, Striker with the Union Local... 29. Mission log: pretty sure I fucked up good.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Got a little farther down and came face-to-face with my "prey." Damn thing was hideous... Was limping along, really feeling the rads at this point.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Didn't feel up to a fight, was pretty sure I was a goner. But it didn't pounce, didn't strike. The thing just... stared. It stared at me.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: It... It knew me, I-I could feel it. How that's possible, I-I don't know, but... sent a chill down my spine.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Its eyes... called to me. Felt like an eternity, but after a minute or two it just, just turned around and left. And so did I.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: I made it back topside. Lucky to be alive, honestly, but all I feel is... is an anger.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: It's swelling up inside me, I'm just, so mad. Mad I didn't kill the thing, mad it didn't kill me. It doesn't make any sense.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Don't-- don't think I'm going back to the 29 any time soon. Need-- need to wait for these urges to subside.

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Don't want to hurt anyone. Shouldn't be near other people right now...

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: God, it's so damn bright up here. Was it always so blinding?

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Need to find a little corner, out of the light. Someplace warm. I don't know why it's gotten so cold, either. Too used to the rads, maybe...

transcript.speaker: Pat Gerber
transcript.text: Gerber out.

entries.title: Nice Work!
entries.text:
It would seem as though they finally hired someone with half a brain if you were able to get passed the password lock I put on this thing.

You're probably looking for all the records I've been supposed to be keeping these past how ever many years. Don't bother. They're gone. All deleted. Shame about that.

My advice to whomever may be reading this. Get out. This job isn't worth it. Couple years in this place will suck your soul dry. Take what's in the safe behind you, tell your bosses you found nothing and run.

If for some reason you decide to stay, remember the company mantra, "blame it on the last guy".

items.name: Terminal — The Pitt - Industrial
items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.title: Entry 00
entries.text:
Looks like I managed to get this thing working again. Ended up having to wipe the entire system though.

Wonder what was on it before?

Shipping records? Payroll slips? HR violations? 

Evidence of a vast conspiracy that reaches the upper levels of the government? 

Yea, probably. Not that any of that matters now.

entries.title: Entry 01
entries.text:
Wow I forgot how satisfying it can be to type on one of these things. Really takes me back to when things were less... shit.

The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog.
The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog.
The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog.
The effervescent brown fox lolloped over the liquescent dog.

Damn, still got it. 

Oh man this stuff's really starting to kick in.

I bet I can get this thing to play Zeta Invaders.

entries.title: Entry 02
entries.text:
My fingers are like the wind. 

My thoughts, expanded infinitely.

The mind is a singularity and we are but minnows swimming upstream in that which we call time.

After all you can't have purple without blue AND red.

When all is one and one are all, we will all truly know The One.

entries.title: Entry 03
entries.text:
Ugh what the hell happened last night? Who the hell is The One? Minnows?

Head hurts like hell, mouth is dry, and I'm pretty sure I threw up some sort of bug meat.

If you're reading this, take the rest of the stash. It's in the safe. I'm done. But don't say I didn't warn you.

For a moment though, everything glowed a just a little bit brighter. Very serene.

entries.title: Welcome to the Union
entries.text:
Well, newcomer, let me be the first to welcome you to the Local 42, the pride of the Union. Our core mission is to protect the Foundry and use its industrial strength to win this war and, eventually, to restore Pittsburgh to its former glory.

It'll be a tough road, but you picked the right side. With us, you get organization, dedication, and democracy. We treat everyone fairly, or strive to. And if you have problems, we have legal outlets to solve them. Most of all, you have a community that cares - about you, and about rebuilding this city into what it used to be.

Skip Roerich
Pittsburgh Union Local 42

entries.title: Our Foundry
entries.text:
The importance of the Foundry cannot be overstated. It is one of the few factories the Union has been able to restore to full working order, and the quality metalwork we produce here give us a critical advantage over the Fanatics. While the loss of the Mill has slowed down production, it has not stopped it entirely. We are still able to feed the fires through the hard work of our field teams, who risk their lives daily to recover the materials we need.

So what does the Foundry do, exactly? The long and short of it is that it takes in metals, melts them down, purifies them, and molds them into the parts we need for equipment. In the ruins of Pittsburgh, we Unioners are the only ones with the know-how to continue this work. A point of pride that no other faction in this "Pitt" of ours can claim.

entries.title: Our enemy
entries.text:
The Fanatics seem monolithic, but in practice they still operate mostly in independent cells, each staking out their own fief centered on some critical piece of infrastructure. While they have enough fundamental understanding to realize the importance of their headquarters, they rarely lack the knowledge to fully operate it. See their occupation of the Mill, once a Union steel mill, now merely a military outpost and torture warehouse under Fanatic rule.

This lack of understanding on their part gives the Union its key advantage: not only do we know the importance of our factories (like this Foundry), but we appreciate it. We may be fewer in number, but our expertise has let us hang on - and in the future, will let us take back Pittsburgh from the chaos.

entries.title: A note to all members
entries.text: Management has been made aware of some disturbing reports filed by workers operating in the lower levels and around the Foundry exterior. In the interest of safety, we ask that for the time being all members pair up for jobs in sectors F-G. We have also chosen to suspend night work for the unpermitted until the Strikers can conduct a full investigation. Thank you for your cooperation.

transcript.speaker: Duchess

transcript.speaker: Gerald Whitehead

transcript.speaker: Duchess

transcript.speaker: Vigilant Citizen
transcript.text: This is... A Vigilant Citizen. And this is an interview with Gladys Filtcher.

transcript.speaker: Vigilant Citizen
transcript.text: Can you repeat that?

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: So those soldiers, they drove onto my land and started fencing off the north part of my farm. Two years back.

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: Well, I ain't one to take that lying down. After making a ruckus, their Captain came by.

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: Said it was for my own safety. That there were dangerous level of radiation over there.

transcript.speaker: Vigilant Citizen
transcript.text: Did they say what caused it?

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: They wouldn't say word one. Before I could carry on too much, this man in a black suit comes over. Says it's eminent domain.

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: And he gives me this check with more zeroes in it that I've ever seen.

transcript.speaker: Vigilant Citizen
transcript.text: Did you take it?

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: Damned right I did. These are hard times.

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: Everyone else I know took the deal, too. We was told to keep it quiet. Not to create a needless panic.

transcript.speaker: Vigilant Citizen
transcript.text: Did you ever see any evidence of the radiation?

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: This is off-the-record. Like you said? Right?

transcript.speaker: Vigilant Citizen
transcript.text: Absolutely. You have my word.

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: *grunt* Well, that's just it. I never saw any signs of anything dangerous.

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: I got a couple cows that like grazing that aways. After the fence, I chased the cows off.

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: But the damned animals always went back.

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: Third time I caught them I gave up. Figured they were goners, anyhow.

transcript.speaker: Vigilant Citizen
transcript.text: So there's no evidence of anything suspicious?

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: No. Truth be told, I almost forgot about it. Except for the noise.

transcript.speaker: Vigilant Citizen
transcript.text: Noise?

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: Yeah, you can hear trucks coming and going every now and then. At the damnedest hours, too.

transcript.speaker: Gladys
transcript.text: A couple times I heard a train whistle, too. But that's about it.

items.name: Filtcher Farm Report
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Dear Leah,

The interview I did with Gladys Filtcher is only part of the story. I followed the fencing for approximately three miles, before I saw a military jeep approaching in the distance.

I couldn't see anything from the fence line. Despite numerous radioactive hazard signs my Geiger Counter did not register anything beyond normal background levels of radiation. Even a minor nuclear accident would register at least something for a massive distance from its source. The upshot is that there clearly was no radioactive accident in that vicinity.

So what was the military doing there? Why was so much land being cordoned off? What were the trucks doing that Mrs. Filtcher reported late at night?

Please use your military contacts to investigate and anonymously publish your findings. If everyone does what they are supposed to the evidence will be undeniable.

Sincerely,
FS

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth White
transcript.text: Sunnytop? Really?

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: I'm not there for the skiing. Or the clientele.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: But I'd rather stay at a shoddy lodge than take my chances with... whatever might be going on down in the valley.

transcript.speaker: Protectron
transcript.text: Ma'am.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: Just set it down. Now, let's finish this rubber. Dollar a point?

items.name: Everything Changes
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: It's funny what comes to mind at a time like this.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: When I was little, I used to come here with my grandfather.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: Every morning, we'd sit right here, have donuts, read the paper. Just the two of us.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: Everything changes. They got rid of the donuts. And the staff. And the whole world.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: But this spot... it's still here.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: Joyce did her best. They all did. I hope they make it out there.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: As for me? I'm going to stay right here. Have one last donut. And whatever happens, happens.

transcript.speaker: Chris Evetts
transcript.text: Everything changes. But in the end? I can't imagine a place I'd rather be.

items.name: Joyce's Message
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: Dave? Dave, honey, it's Joyce.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: I... I don't know if you'll ever get this. But I wanted to make sure there was something here, if you came looking, if you made it.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: God, where to start?

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: It's... it's about two-thirty in the morning. New Year's. 2079.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: I've been here for the past year, since the war. Me, a couple of the staff, about a hundred guests. And the robots.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: Never thought I'd be grateful for the robots.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: We made out all right. Even made me manager. Can you believe it?

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: But... we have to go. Paula and I, we're leaving for Charleston in the morning.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: I've missed you and the girls. Missed you so, so much. Take care of them for me, all right?

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: All my love. Always.

items.name: One Last Toast
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: All right, all right, settle down.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: I know the last few weeks have been a shock. We all hoped we could stay here forever.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: But when you stop and think about it, we've been blessed. So many people have had it so much worse.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: For the past year, The Whitespring has been our home. A shelter from the storm just outside the gates.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: It's time for us to face that storm.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: But we're ready. Ready, like none of us was on that day.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: We've had time to plan, to prepare, to stock up. To find friends to share the road ahead.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: The Whitespring bought us that time. Let's make the most of it.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: Ladies and Gentlemen, one last toast. To The Whitespring.

items.name: Springhill Feedback

location.text: Found near The Whitespring North Entrance.

items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: Mr. Ainsley. I wanted to remark upon the fascinating design of your new Springhill golf course.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: You appear to have seven holes. Seven. What a curious number.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: Nine, I could understand. Or perhaps six, played thrice. But... seven.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: Most courses put ever so much effort into varying their holes. You appear to have liked your third so much, you repeated it immediately.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: Or take the cart paths. One normally takes such little note of them.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: I had a wonderful chance to reflect on that during the three-mile drive from the fifth hole to the sixth.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: And then, seven. Ah, seven. Such a slope. It would make a fabulous ski run.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: Not that teeing off with a four hundred yard putt wasn't a unique experience.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: I confess, when I heard you had carved up your championship golf course for housing tracts, I was concerned it might have impacted the quality a little.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: Clearly, I underestimated the scope of your ambition.

transcript.speaker: Henrietta Winchester
transcript.text: Cordially yours. Henrietta Winchester.

items.name: The Whitespring Staff Meeting, 12.27.79
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: And... recording. All right. What are we looking at?

transcript.speaker: Lew Palmest
transcript.text: I've got nothing.

transcript.speaker: Paula Hamilton
transcript.text: Really, Lew? Really? You set up the damn things. Don't tell me you don't know how to hack them.

transcript.speaker: Paula Hamilton
transcript.text: Can't you just shut them off? Or keep them from turning on us? There has to be a way.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: Paula-

transcript.speaker: Lew Palmest
transcript.text: No. Really, no. I'm sorry, Paula. We've tried everything.

transcript.speaker: Lew Palmest
transcript.text: Not just me, every guest who can work a terminal. We've been locked out. We're getting kicked out. And there's nothing we can do.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: Paula, how's the training going?

transcript.speaker: Paula Hamilton
transcript.text: Friedrich's classes are a joke, but the guests have been pitching in.

transcript.speaker: Paula Hamilton
transcript.text: The Warrens picked up a few things on safari. Sgt. Tommelson's been teaching marksmanship.

transcript.speaker: Lew Palmest
transcript.text: Tommelson? That crank who thinks the communists are bugging his room?

transcript.speaker: Paula Hamilton
transcript.text: Yeah. Best we got.

transcript.speaker: Lew Palmest
transcript.text: God.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: At least people have been stocking up. The 'All-You-Can-Carry' Shopping Spree was a hit. No one turned that down.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: Anyone have anything else? Robert, how're things?

transcript.speaker: Robert Mitchell
transcript.text: Keepin' on.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: Good. The Gala's on Sunday, so this may be our last staff meeting.

transcript.speaker: Joyce Easton
transcript.text: Whatever happens... we did all we could, this past year. I couldn't have done it without you. Thank you.

items.name: They're Coming

location.text: Found near The Whitespring Golf Club.

items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Lew Palmest
transcript.text: They keep coming. They, they just keep coming.

transcript.speaker: Lew Palmest
transcript.text: Rob. Rob saw them first. Three. Just, just three, out on the Seventh. Easy shots from up here.

transcript.speaker: Lew Palmest
transcript.text: At first, we thought it was fun. Tried to see who could, who could pick them off. Extra points for the head.

transcript.speaker: Lew Palmest
transcript.text: Then, then Rob went missing. Went down to the range. Wasn't far. Wasn't, wasn't back by dark.

transcript.speaker: Lew Palmest
transcript.text: Then Ted. Zack. Zack, Phil, Mark. God, Mark. They dragged him. I can, can still hear him screaming.

transcript.speaker: Lew Palmest
transcript.text: Now we're three. Just, just three. Can't run. Can't hold. Can't.

transcript.speaker: Lew Palmest
transcript.text: They're, they're coming. They're coming!
